intended_object: For an ℕ-graded ring A and a ring map f : A → B, the extension f(A₊)B of the irrelevant ideal A₊ = ⊕_{n>0} Aₙ, i.e. the ideal of B generated by images of positive-degree homogeneous elements (from the docstring and its use as the ideal cutting out the complement of the domain of a degree-scaled Proj map).
explanation: The body is `Ideal.map f (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal`. `Ideal.map` is the ideal generated by the image, and Mathlib's irrelevant ideal is the span of the positive-degree homogeneous elements. So this is exactly the ideal generated by the images of all positive homogeneous forms, as the docstring says. The lemma `degreeScaledDomain_eq_zeroLocus_compl` in the same file confirms the intended meaning. Generality: the ℕ-grading on A is inherited from Mathlib's `HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant`, and B needs no grading here (the grading ℬ is not used in the body). The shared universe for A and B is a file-wide setting needed elsewhere and is harmless. Mathlib has no dedicated name for this extended ideal; the definition is a correct combination of `Ideal.map` and `HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant`.
